candidates: testsuite/integration-arquillian/tests/base/src/test/java/org/keycloak/testsuite/AssertEvents.java:482 - isAccessTokenId never checks the grant shortcut: wrong offset and inverted condition.. The grant shortcut is the last 2 of the 6 prefix characters (`substring(4, 6)`), but the matcher reads `substring(3, 5)`, which for `onrtac` gives `ta`. The condition is also inverted: it returns false when the shortcut *matches*. Together, the comparison never matches, so any `xxxxxx:<uuid>` id passes no matter which grant issued it. The CODE_TO_TOKEN, REFRESH, device and CIBA assertions therefore never check the grant type. A prefix shorter than 5 characters throws StringIndexOutOfBoundsException instead of returning false. Fix: `if (items[0].length() != 6 || !items[0].substring(4, 6).equals(expectedGrantShortcut)) return false;`.

server-spi-private/src/main/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/grants/OAuth2GrantTypeFactory.java:33 - New abstract getShortcut() breaks existing custom grant-type factories and can stop the server from starting.. `getShortcut()` is added to the public `OAuth2GrantTypeFactory` SPI with no default. An already compiled third-party grant factory will throw AbstractMethodError when `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.postInit` calls it. A factory that returns null will throw NullPointerException from `ConcurrentHashMap.put`. In both cases postInit fails and the server does not start. Give the method a default (for example, derived from the id, or null handled as 'na') and skip or log factories without a usable shortcut instead of failing at startup.

services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/encode/AccessTokenContext.java:73 - The null check meant for rawTokenId checks grantType again.. `Objects.requireNonNull(grantType, "Null rawTokenId not allowed")` checks `grantType` a second time, so a null `rawTokenId` is accepted. `encodeTokenId` would then produce an id like `onrtac:null`. Change it to `Objects.requireNonNull(rawTokenId, ...)`.
